artifacts.summary: Three-phase plan adding SESSION_LOCK_CONTENTION, HOOK_REGEX_BOUNDARY_DEFECT, and DEPLOY_ORPHAN_DRIFT to the defect_class enum in system-defect-record.sh and the Signal A table in system-defect-discrimination.md, with a cross-file round-trip verification phase.

memory_candidates.content: Widening a closed string enum in this agent system has a narrow, verifiable blast radius when every consumer is a producer of fixed literals rather than a dispatcher over the enum. The defect_class vocabulary is the worked example: it is validated in exactly one place (a bash `case` arm in scripts/system-defect-record.sh) and defined in exactly one place (the Signal A table in context/patterns/system-defect-discrimination.md), while ~17 call sites across skill-base.sh, five hooks, and two orchestrate SKILL.md files each pass one hardcoded literal. Because no call site branches on the enum, additive widening requires zero consumer edits. Two audit lessons: (1) grep the flag spelling (`--defect-class`), not just the variable spelling (`defect_class`) -- the underscore grep found 4 files, the hyphen grep found 8, and only the wider set proves the no-dispatch claim; (2) count words embedded in prose and error messages ('one of the ten Signal A instances') are part of the enum's surface area and drift silently, so grep for the spelled-out count alongside the values. Vocabulary naming and detector wiring are deliberately separate, sequential tasks here -- a class may legitimately sit in the enum marked 'not currently computed anywhere'.
